CVE-2026-59774.title: Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read can lead to RCE
CVE-2026-59774.description: ### Summary An unauthenticated remote attacker can submit Org-mode markup containing a #+INCLUDE directive to POST /{owner}/{repo}/markup for any suitable public repository to read arbitrary server files. By extracting INTERNAL_TOKEN from app.ini, they can inject a Git hook through the internal logger and achieve command execution as the Gitea OS user during an anonymous clone. ### Details Gitea registers `POST /{username}/{reponame}/markup` with optional sign-in, repository assignment, and a repository-unit reader check. An anonymous user passes that check for a public repository with a normal readable code unit. The handler passes the supplied `Mode`, `Text`, and `FilePath` into Gitea's generic markup renderer. Selecting `Mode: file` and a `.org` filename chooses the Org-mode renderer. Gitea 1.27.0 initializes `go-org` using `org.New()` and does not replace its default `ReadFile` callback. In `go-org` 1.9.1, that callback is `ioutil.ReadFile`; `#+INCLUDE` accepts absolute paths and passes them directly to that callback. #### Preconditions - At least one repository is publicly readable and exposes a unit accepted by the repository markup route. A normal public repository with its code unit enabled satisfies this condition. - Standard Gitea storage permissions allow the service user to update Gitea's managed global Git configuration. ### Impact - Read arbitrary files accessible to the Gitea service user without an account. - Submit the file-read payload directly through a public repository's web markup route without committing a file or obtaining repository write access. - Expose Gitea configuration, internal bearer tokens, OAuth/JWT material, and deployment metadata ### Affected - The vulnerable version seem v1.22.1 ~ v1.27.0 ### Credit Found by @xbow-security. Triaged by Guido Leo <guido.leo@xbow.com>. Independently reported by https://github.com/NightRang3r

An earlier advisory fixed the corresponding team-side endpoint; the repository-side endpoint retained the weaker check. ### Details The repository-side handler's exception relies on a repository permission check (`IsOwner()`), which for an organization repository is satisfied by a user promoted to owner-level access through an attached admin team. The fixed team-side endpoint instead checks actual organization ownership when `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess` is disabled. The matching web collaboration-settings handler had the same weak check. ### Impact A user with delegated admin rights on one organization repository can grant other organization teams read or write access to that repository without approval from an actual organization owner, exposing private source and history and, for a write-capable team, granting push access. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39046, #39058). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-60018.title: Authenticated DoS in OneDev migration via unbounded version response body
CVE-2026-60018.description: ### Summary The OneDev migration downloader reads the entire `/~api/version/server` response body into memory before validating the version string, and the migration HTTP client has no timeout. A malicious OneDev-compatible server can return a very large or never-ending response. ### Details Reachable from the web, API and background-task migration paths. Reachable by any authenticated user who can start a repository migration. ### Impact Authenticated availability. An attacker who can start migrations against a server they control can force Gitea to read arbitrarily large response bodies, hold migration requests and workers open until timeout or cancellation, retain that data in memory, and exhaust the migration worker pool. On constrained deployments this creates memory pressure and a possible out-of-memory condition. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.16.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39024, #39033). ### Workarounds Restrict repository-migration permission to trusted users. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-63792.title: Fork pull requests can read reusable workflow files from another private repository (missed sibling of GHSA-fj8v-hjwv-qm88)
CVE-2026-63792.description: ### Summary `CanReadWorkflowCrossRepo` decides whether an Actions run may read a reusable workflow file referenced from another repository. Its 'collaborative owner' branch grants cross-repository read through the collaborative-owner trust relationship without checking whether the run is a fork pull request. An earlier advisory fixed the same class of flaw in a sibling function but did not touch this one. ### Details A fork pull request opened against private repository A (no write access to A required) can read reusable workflow file contents of a different private repository B, at any git ref, provided A is private, B's Actions configuration lists A's owner as a collaborative owner (a normal use of the reusable-workflow sharing feature), and the fork pull request run is approved and runs. The workflow file path is confined to the configured workflow directories, but the git ref is caller-controlled. ### Impact Read-only disclosure of private reusable workflow file contents. No write access or code execution is granted by this issue. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-66877.title: RCE on self-hosted runners | fork-PR approval gate (`NeedApproval`) bypass via job-level concurrency cancellation
CVE-2026-66877.description: ### Summary Workflow runs from first-time fork contributors are held for maintainer approval only by inserting the run's jobs in a blocked state. The component that transitions blocked jobs to waiting does not re-check whether the run still needs approval. A separate, legitimate run in the same repository that shares a job-level `concurrency` group with the pending run can cause the pending run to be re-evaluated, which unblocks and dispatches its remaining jobs to runners without approval. Any user who can open a pull request can reach this. ### Details The approval decision itself is correct, but it is enforced purely as job status. The job emitter, the concurrency-preparation path and the runner task-pickup path do not check approval; only the concurrency-wake path did. Cancelling one job of the pending run through the shared job-level concurrency group triggers a re-emit over that run's still-blocked sibling jobs, which are then moved to waiting and picked up by runners. ### Impact Arbitrary, unreviewed workflow code execution on the self-hosted runners of any repository that accepts fork pull requests, defeating the first-time-contributor approval boundary. Fork pull request secrets remain withheld and the run token remains read-only; the impact is access to the runner host (internal network reachability, runner-local caches, workspaces and credentials, and persistence into later trusted builds). ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-71184.title: Gitea Actions: fork pull request approval bypass via `pull_request_review_comment` (missing `WithPullRequest`)
CVE-2026-71184.description: ### Summary Gitea requires maintainer approval before running fork pull request workflows when the author lacks Actions write on the base repository. That gate is skipped for the `pull_request_review_comment` event (the same code path also covers review approved/rejected), because the review notifier does not attach the pull request to the notification. With no pull request attached the run is not recognized as a fork pull request and approval is not required, while the workflow definition is still loaded from the fork head and run on the base repository's runners. ### Details The sibling review-request notifier does attach the pull request; the review notifier does not. Present since the fork pull request approval gate was introduced in Gitea 1.20.0. An actor needs to be able to fork the repository, open a fork pull request, and submit a review with a line comment; they do not need Actions write on the base repository or a runner on the fork. ### Impact Unapproved execution of attacker-controlled workflow code on the base repository's runners. On a privileged or host runner this is code execution as the runner user, with possible access to secrets depending on event rules; on a sandboxed runner it is unauthorized CI/compute use. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.20.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73130.title: Unbounded gitignores repository-creation field enables linear template-read amplification
CVE-2026-73130.description: ### Summary The `gitignores` field of the repository-creation form and API option struct has no maximum-length constraint. During repository initialization the field is split on commas and each name triggers a template read whose result is buffered in memory before `.gitignore` is written. A large attacker-controlled value therefore produces a proportional number of template reads and in-memory buffering. ### Details Reachable through `POST /repo/create` and `POST /api/v1/user/repos` (and the organization equivalent) when auto-init is enabled. ### Impact Uncontrolled resource consumption during repository creation, proportional to the submitted field length. Availability only. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39027, #39040). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73273.title: Package size quota bypass and unbounded memory read in the Maven checksum upload path
CVE-2026-73273.description: ### Summary When a Maven artifact is uploaded with a checksum extension (`.md5`, `.sha1`, `.sha256`, `.sha512`), the handler reads the entire request body into memory and compares it to the stored digest, then returns — before the code path that enforces the package size quota. The checksum branch therefore has neither a size quota nor any bound on how much is read into memory, although a valid checksum value is at most 128 bytes. ### Details The body is read with `io.ReadAll` and copied again for the comparison; both allocations are sized by the client. The configured `LIMIT_SIZE_MAVEN` is not applied to this path. Reachable by any authenticated user with Maven package write access. ### Impact Package size-quota bypass and client-controlled memory allocation for a single request (uncontrolled resource consumption). A practical outage was not demonstrated; the issue should be read as an unbounded allocation and a quota bypass. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39028, #39031). ### Workarounds Limit request body size at the reverse proxy. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73278.title: WebAuthn second factor is bypassed on OAuth2/OpenID sign-in (WebAuthn-only users)
CVE-2026-73278.description: Gitea's OAuth2 and OpenID Connect sign-in flows did not enforce WebAuthn when it was a user's only configured second factor. Users who registered a passkey without TOTP were correctly challenged on password login, but could receive a full authenticated session through OAuth sign-in with no WebAuthn prompt. Two OAuth-related code paths were affected. One of them could also persist an external identity link during sign-in, extending the impact beyond a single session. ## Affected Versions All versions up to and including **1.27.0** that support WebAuthn and OAuth2/OpenID sign-in. ## Impact **Who was affected:** Users who used WebAuthn as their sole second factor (no TOTP enrolled) and signed in through an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider. **What broke:** WebAuthn is intended to protect accounts when another credential (such as a password or a compromised identity provider session) is known or stolen. On the affected OAuth paths, that protection was not applied. Password-based login continued to enforce the passkey challenge as expected. | Path | Scenario | Consequence | |------|----------|-------------| | Linked-identity OAuth callback | Attacker authenticates with a victim's already-linked external identity | Full session without WebAuthn challenge | | OAuth account-link sign-in | Attacker links an external identity to a victim account using the victim's password | Full session without WebAuthn challenge; external identity permanently linked to the victim account | The account-link path was the more serious case: a successful sign-in could bind the attacker's identity provider account to the victim's Gitea account. Subsequent OAuth sign-ins through that provider might no longer require the victim's password, and password rotation alone might not revoke that access. This issue is separate from [CVE-2026-20779](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-20779), which addressed TOTP replay timing. This advisory concerns which second factors the OAuth sign-in paths considered before granting a session. ## Root Cause OAuth sign-in handlers determined whether second-factor verification was required by consulting TOTP enrollment only (`GetTwoFactorByUID`). WebAuthn credentials are stored separately and were not checked on those paths before a session was issued. The password login handler already checked both TOTP and WebAuthn enrollment and redirected to the WebAuthn challenge when appropriate. A combined helper (`HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn`) existed in the codebase but was not used to gate session creation on the affected OAuth handlers. **Affected components:** - `routers/web/auth/oauth.go` — linked-identity callback (`handleOAuth2SignIn`) - `routers/web/auth/linkaccount.go` — account-link sign-in (`oauth2LinkAccount`) **Reference implementation (correct behavior):** - `routers/web/auth/auth.go` — password login path

CVE-2026-59774.title: Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read can lead to RCE
CVE-2026-59774.description: ### Summary An unauthenticated remote attacker can submit Org-mode markup containing a #+INCLUDE directive to POST /{owner}/{repo}/markup for any suitable public repository to read arbitrary server files. By extracting INTERNAL_TOKEN from app.ini, they can inject a Git hook through the internal logger and achieve command execution as the Gitea OS user during an anonymous clone. ### Details Gitea registers `POST /{username}/{reponame}/markup` with optional sign-in, repository assignment, and a repository-unit reader check. An anonymous user passes that check for a public repository with a normal readable code unit. The handler passes the supplied `Mode`, `Text`, and `FilePath` into Gitea's generic markup renderer. Selecting `Mode: file` and a `.org` filename chooses the Org-mode renderer. Gitea 1.27.0 initializes `go-org` using `org.New()` and does not replace its default `ReadFile` callback. In `go-org` 1.9.1, that callback is `ioutil.ReadFile`; `#+INCLUDE` accepts absolute paths and passes them directly to that callback. #### Preconditions - At least one repository is publicly readable and exposes a unit accepted by the repository markup route. A normal public repository with its code unit enabled satisfies this condition. - Standard Gitea storage permissions allow the service user to update Gitea's managed global Git configuration. ### Impact - Read arbitrary files accessible to the Gitea service user without an account. - Submit the file-read payload directly through a public repository's web markup route without committing a file or obtaining repository write access. - Expose Gitea configuration, internal bearer tokens, OAuth/JWT material, and deployment metadata ### Affected - The vulnerable version seem v1.22.1 ~ v1.27.0 ### Credit Found by @xbow-security. Triaged by Guido Leo <guido.leo@xbow.com>. Independently reported by https://github.com/NightRang3r

CVE-2026-60010.title: Repo-side team-link endpoint still bypasses RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess
CVE-2026-60010.description: ### Summary `PUT /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/teams/{team}` allows a non-owner repository admin to attach organization teams to a repository even when the organization has disabled that behaviour with `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess=false`. An earlier advisory fixed the corresponding team-side endpoint; the repository-side endpoint retained the weaker check. ### Details The repository-side handler's exception relies on a repository permission check (`IsOwner()`), which for an organization repository is satisfied by a user promoted to owner-level access through an attached admin team. The fixed team-side endpoint instead checks actual organization ownership when `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess` is disabled. The matching web collaboration-settings handler had the same weak check. ### Impact A user with delegated admin rights on one organization repository can grant other organization teams read or write access to that repository without approval from an actual organization owner, exposing private source and history and, for a write-capable team, granting push access. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39046, #39058). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-60018.title: Authenticated DoS in OneDev migration via unbounded version response body
CVE-2026-60018.description: ### Summary The OneDev migration downloader reads the entire `/~api/version/server` response body into memory before validating the version string, and the migration HTTP client has no timeout. A malicious OneDev-compatible server can return a very large or never-ending response. ### Details Reachable from the web, API and background-task migration paths. Reachable by any authenticated user who can start a repository migration. ### Impact Authenticated availability. An attacker who can start migrations against a server they control can force Gitea to read arbitrarily large response bodies, hold migration requests and workers open until timeout or cancellation, retain that data in memory, and exhaust the migration worker pool. On constrained deployments this creates memory pressure and a possible out-of-memory condition. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.16.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39024, #39033). ### Workarounds Restrict repository-migration permission to trusted users. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-63792.title: Fork pull requests can read reusable workflow files from another private repository (missed sibling of GHSA-fj8v-hjwv-qm88)
CVE-2026-63792.description: ### Summary `CanReadWorkflowCrossRepo` decides whether an Actions run may read a reusable workflow file referenced from another repository. Its 'collaborative owner' branch grants cross-repository read through the collaborative-owner trust relationship without checking whether the run is a fork pull request. An earlier advisory fixed the same class of flaw in a sibling function but did not touch this one. ### Details A fork pull request opened against private repository A (no write access to A required) can read reusable workflow file contents of a different private repository B, at any git ref, provided A is private, B's Actions configuration lists A's owner as a collaborative owner (a normal use of the reusable-workflow sharing feature), and the fork pull request run is approved and runs. The workflow file path is confined to the configured workflow directories, but the git ref is caller-controlled. ### Impact Read-only disclosure of private reusable workflow file contents. No write access or code execution is granted by this issue. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-66877.title: RCE on self-hosted runners | fork-PR approval gate (`NeedApproval`) bypass via job-level concurrency cancellation
CVE-2026-66877.description: ### Summary Workflow runs from first-time fork contributors are held for maintainer approval only by inserting the run's jobs in a blocked state. The component that transitions blocked jobs to waiting does not re-check whether the run still needs approval. A separate, legitimate run in the same repository that shares a job-level `concurrency` group with the pending run can cause the pending run to be re-evaluated, which unblocks and dispatches its remaining jobs to runners without approval. Any user who can open a pull request can reach this. ### Details The approval decision itself is correct, but it is enforced purely as job status. The job emitter, the concurrency-preparation path and the runner task-pickup path do not check approval; only the concurrency-wake path did. Cancelling one job of the pending run through the shared job-level concurrency group triggers a re-emit over that run's still-blocked sibling jobs, which are then moved to waiting and picked up by runners. ### Impact Arbitrary, unreviewed workflow code execution on the self-hosted runners of any repository that accepts fork pull requests, defeating the first-time-contributor approval boundary. Fork pull request secrets remain withheld and the run token remains read-only; the impact is access to the runner host (internal network reachability, runner-local caches, workspaces and credentials, and persistence into later trusted builds). ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-71184.title: Gitea Actions: fork pull request approval bypass via `pull_request_review_comment` (missing `WithPullRequest`)
CVE-2026-71184.description: ### Summary Gitea requires maintainer approval before running fork pull request workflows when the author lacks Actions write on the base repository. That gate is skipped for the `pull_request_review_comment` event (the same code path also covers review approved/rejected), because the review notifier does not attach the pull request to the notification. With no pull request attached the run is not recognized as a fork pull request and approval is not required, while the workflow definition is still loaded from the fork head and run on the base repository's runners. ### Details The sibling review-request notifier does attach the pull request; the review notifier does not. Present since the fork pull request approval gate was introduced in Gitea 1.20.0. An actor needs to be able to fork the repository, open a fork pull request, and submit a review with a line comment; they do not need Actions write on the base repository or a runner on the fork. ### Impact Unapproved execution of attacker-controlled workflow code on the base repository's runners. On a privileged or host runner this is code execution as the runner user, with possible access to secrets depending on event rules; on a sandboxed runner it is unauthorized CI/compute use. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.20.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73130.title: Unbounded gitignores repository-creation field enables linear template-read amplification
CVE-2026-73130.description: ### Summary The `gitignores` field of the repository-creation form and API option struct has no maximum-length constraint. During repository initialization the field is split on commas and each name triggers a template read whose result is buffered in memory before `.gitignore` is written. A large attacker-controlled value therefore produces a proportional number of template reads and in-memory buffering. ### Details Reachable through `POST /repo/create` and `POST /api/v1/user/repos` (and the organization equivalent) when auto-init is enabled. ### Impact Uncontrolled resource consumption during repository creation, proportional to the submitted field length. Availability only. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39027, #39040). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73273.title: Package size quota bypass and unbounded memory read in the Maven checksum upload path
CVE-2026-73273.description: ### Summary When a Maven artifact is uploaded with a checksum extension (`.md5`, `.sha1`, `.sha256`, `.sha512`), the handler reads the entire request body into memory and compares it to the stored digest, then returns — before the code path that enforces the package size quota. The checksum branch therefore has neither a size quota nor any bound on how much is read into memory, although a valid checksum value is at most 128 bytes. ### Details The body is read with `io.ReadAll` and copied again for the comparison; both allocations are sized by the client. The configured `LIMIT_SIZE_MAVEN` is not applied to this path. Reachable by any authenticated user with Maven package write access. ### Impact Package size-quota bypass and client-controlled memory allocation for a single request (uncontrolled resource consumption). A practical outage was not demonstrated; the issue should be read as an unbounded allocation and a quota bypass. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39028, #39031). ### Workarounds Limit request body size at the reverse proxy. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73278.title: WebAuthn second factor is bypassed on OAuth2/OpenID sign-in (WebAuthn-only users)
CVE-2026-73278.description: Gitea's OAuth2 and OpenID Connect sign-in flows did not enforce WebAuthn when it was a user's only configured second factor. Users who registered a passkey without TOTP were correctly challenged on password login, but could receive a full authenticated session through OAuth sign-in with no WebAuthn prompt. Two OAuth-related code paths were affected. One of them could also persist an external identity link during sign-in, extending the impact beyond a single session. ## Affected Versions All versions up to and including **1.27.0** that support WebAuthn and OAuth2/OpenID sign-in. ## Impact **Who was affected:** Users who used WebAuthn as their sole second factor (no TOTP enrolled) and signed in through an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider. **What broke:** WebAuthn is intended to protect accounts when another credential (such as a password or a compromised identity provider session) is known or stolen. On the affected OAuth paths, that protection was not applied. Password-based login continued to enforce the passkey challenge as expected. | Path | Scenario | Consequence | |------|----------|-------------| | Linked-identity OAuth callback | Attacker authenticates with a victim's already-linked external identity | Full session without WebAuthn challenge | | OAuth account-link sign-in | Attacker links an external identity to a victim account using the victim's password | Full session without WebAuthn challenge; external identity permanently linked to the victim account | The account-link path was the more serious case: a successful sign-in could bind the attacker's identity provider account to the victim's Gitea account. Subsequent OAuth sign-ins through that provider might no longer require the victim's password, and password rotation alone might not revoke that access. This issue is separate from [CVE-2026-20779](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-20779), which addressed TOTP replay timing. This advisory concerns which second factors the OAuth sign-in paths considered before granting a session. ## Root Cause OAuth sign-in handlers determined whether second-factor verification was required by consulting TOTP enrollment only (`GetTwoFactorByUID`). WebAuthn credentials are stored separately and were not checked on those paths before a session was issued. The password login handler already checked both TOTP and WebAuthn enrollment and redirected to the WebAuthn challenge when appropriate. A combined helper (`HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn`) existed in the codebase but was not used to gate session creation on the affected OAuth handlers. **Affected components:** - `routers/web/auth/oauth.go` — linked-identity callback (`handleOAuth2SignIn`) - `routers/web/auth/linkaccount.go` — account-link sign-in (`oauth2LinkAccount`) **Reference implementation (correct behavior):** - `routers/web/auth/auth.go` — password login path

CVE-2026-59774.title: Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read can lead to RCE
CVE-2026-59774.description: ### Summary An unauthenticated remote attacker can submit Org-mode markup containing a #+INCLUDE directive to POST /{owner}/{repo}/markup for any suitable public repository to read arbitrary server files. By extracting INTERNAL_TOKEN from app.ini, they can inject a Git hook through the internal logger and achieve command execution as the Gitea OS user during an anonymous clone. ### Details Gitea registers `POST /{username}/{reponame}/markup` with optional sign-in, repository assignment, and a repository-unit reader check. An anonymous user passes that check for a public repository with a normal readable code unit. The handler passes the supplied `Mode`, `Text`, and `FilePath` into Gitea's generic markup renderer. Selecting `Mode: file` and a `.org` filename chooses the Org-mode renderer. Gitea 1.27.0 initializes `go-org` using `org.New()` and does not replace its default `ReadFile` callback. In `go-org` 1.9.1, that callback is `ioutil.ReadFile`; `#+INCLUDE` accepts absolute paths and passes them directly to that callback. #### Preconditions - At least one repository is publicly readable and exposes a unit accepted by the repository markup route. A normal public repository with its code unit enabled satisfies this condition. - Standard Gitea storage permissions allow the service user to update Gitea's managed global Git configuration. ### Impact - Read arbitrary files accessible to the Gitea service user without an account. - Submit the file-read payload directly through a public repository's web markup route without committing a file or obtaining repository write access. - Expose Gitea configuration, internal bearer tokens, OAuth/JWT material, and deployment metadata ### Affected - The vulnerable version seem v1.22.1 ~ v1.27.0 ### Credit Found by @xbow-security. Triaged by Guido Leo <guido.leo@xbow.com>. Independently reported by https://github.com/NightRang3r

CVE-2026-60010.title: Repo-side team-link endpoint still bypasses RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess
CVE-2026-60010.description: ### Summary `PUT /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/teams/{team}` allows a non-owner repository admin to attach organization teams to a repository even when the organization has disabled that behaviour with `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess=false`. An earlier advisory fixed the corresponding team-side endpoint; the repository-side endpoint retained the weaker check. ### Details The repository-side handler's exception relies on a repository permission check (`IsOwner()`), which for an organization repository is satisfied by a user promoted to owner-level access through an attached admin team. The fixed team-side endpoint instead checks actual organization ownership when `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess` is disabled. The matching web collaboration-settings handler had the same weak check. ### Impact A user with delegated admin rights on one organization repository can grant other organization teams read or write access to that repository without approval from an actual organization owner, exposing private source and history and, for a write-capable team, granting push access. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39046, #39058). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-60018.title: Authenticated DoS in OneDev migration via unbounded version response body
CVE-2026-60018.description: ### Summary The OneDev migration downloader reads the entire `/~api/version/server` response body into memory before validating the version string, and the migration HTTP client has no timeout. A malicious OneDev-compatible server can return a very large or never-ending response. ### Details Reachable from the web, API and background-task migration paths. Reachable by any authenticated user who can start a repository migration. ### Impact Authenticated availability. An attacker who can start migrations against a server they control can force Gitea to read arbitrarily large response bodies, hold migration requests and workers open until timeout or cancellation, retain that data in memory, and exhaust the migration worker pool. On constrained deployments this creates memory pressure and a possible out-of-memory condition. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.16.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39024, #39033). ### Workarounds Restrict repository-migration permission to trusted users. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-63792.title: Fork pull requests can read reusable workflow files from another private repository (missed sibling of GHSA-fj8v-hjwv-qm88)
CVE-2026-63792.description: ### Summary `CanReadWorkflowCrossRepo` decides whether an Actions run may read a reusable workflow file referenced from another repository. Its 'collaborative owner' branch grants cross-repository read through the collaborative-owner trust relationship without checking whether the run is a fork pull request. An earlier advisory fixed the same class of flaw in a sibling function but did not touch this one. ### Details A fork pull request opened against private repository A (no write access to A required) can read reusable workflow file contents of a different private repository B, at any git ref, provided A is private, B's Actions configuration lists A's owner as a collaborative owner (a normal use of the reusable-workflow sharing feature), and the fork pull request run is approved and runs. The workflow file path is confined to the configured workflow directories, but the git ref is caller-controlled. ### Impact Read-only disclosure of private reusable workflow file contents. No write access or code execution is granted by this issue. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-66877.title: RCE on self-hosted runners | fork-PR approval gate (`NeedApproval`) bypass via job-level concurrency cancellation
CVE-2026-66877.description: ### Summary Workflow runs from first-time fork contributors are held for maintainer approval only by inserting the run's jobs in a blocked state. The component that transitions blocked jobs to waiting does not re-check whether the run still needs approval. A separate, legitimate run in the same repository that shares a job-level `concurrency` group with the pending run can cause the pending run to be re-evaluated, which unblocks and dispatches its remaining jobs to runners without approval. Any user who can open a pull request can reach this. ### Details The approval decision itself is correct, but it is enforced purely as job status. The job emitter, the concurrency-preparation path and the runner task-pickup path do not check approval; only the concurrency-wake path did. Cancelling one job of the pending run through the shared job-level concurrency group triggers a re-emit over that run's still-blocked sibling jobs, which are then moved to waiting and picked up by runners. ### Impact Arbitrary, unreviewed workflow code execution on the self-hosted runners of any repository that accepts fork pull requests, defeating the first-time-contributor approval boundary. Fork pull request secrets remain withheld and the run token remains read-only; the impact is access to the runner host (internal network reachability, runner-local caches, workspaces and credentials, and persistence into later trusted builds). ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-71184.title: Gitea Actions: fork pull request approval bypass via `pull_request_review_comment` (missing `WithPullRequest`)
CVE-2026-71184.description: ### Summary Gitea requires maintainer approval before running fork pull request workflows when the author lacks Actions write on the base repository. That gate is skipped for the `pull_request_review_comment` event (the same code path also covers review approved/rejected), because the review notifier does not attach the pull request to the notification. With no pull request attached the run is not recognized as a fork pull request and approval is not required, while the workflow definition is still loaded from the fork head and run on the base repository's runners. ### Details The sibling review-request notifier does attach the pull request; the review notifier does not. Present since the fork pull request approval gate was introduced in Gitea 1.20.0. An actor needs to be able to fork the repository, open a fork pull request, and submit a review with a line comment; they do not need Actions write on the base repository or a runner on the fork. ### Impact Unapproved execution of attacker-controlled workflow code on the base repository's runners. On a privileged or host runner this is code execution as the runner user, with possible access to secrets depending on event rules; on a sandboxed runner it is unauthorized CI/compute use. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.20.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73130.title: Unbounded gitignores repository-creation field enables linear template-read amplification
CVE-2026-73130.description: ### Summary The `gitignores` field of the repository-creation form and API option struct has no maximum-length constraint. During repository initialization the field is split on commas and each name triggers a template read whose result is buffered in memory before `.gitignore` is written. A large attacker-controlled value therefore produces a proportional number of template reads and in-memory buffering. ### Details Reachable through `POST /repo/create` and `POST /api/v1/user/repos` (and the organization equivalent) when auto-init is enabled. ### Impact Uncontrolled resource consumption during repository creation, proportional to the submitted field length. Availability only. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39027, #39040). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73273.title: Package size quota bypass and unbounded memory read in the Maven checksum upload path
CVE-2026-73273.description: ### Summary When a Maven artifact is uploaded with a checksum extension (`.md5`, `.sha1`, `.sha256`, `.sha512`), the handler reads the entire request body into memory and compares it to the stored digest, then returns — before the code path that enforces the package size quota. The checksum branch therefore has neither a size quota nor any bound on how much is read into memory, although a valid checksum value is at most 128 bytes. ### Details The body is read with `io.ReadAll` and copied again for the comparison; both allocations are sized by the client. The configured `LIMIT_SIZE_MAVEN` is not applied to this path. Reachable by any authenticated user with Maven package write access. ### Impact Package size-quota bypass and client-controlled memory allocation for a single request (uncontrolled resource consumption). A practical outage was not demonstrated; the issue should be read as an unbounded allocation and a quota bypass. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39028, #39031). ### Workarounds Limit request body size at the reverse proxy. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73278.title: WebAuthn second factor is bypassed on OAuth2/OpenID sign-in (WebAuthn-only users)
CVE-2026-73278.description: Gitea's OAuth2 and OpenID Connect sign-in flows did not enforce WebAuthn when it was a user's only configured second factor. Users who registered a passkey without TOTP were correctly challenged on password login, but could receive a full authenticated session through OAuth sign-in with no WebAuthn prompt. Two OAuth-related code paths were affected. One of them could also persist an external identity link during sign-in, extending the impact beyond a single session. ## Affected Versions All versions up to and including **1.27.0** that support WebAuthn and OAuth2/OpenID sign-in. ## Impact **Who was affected:** Users who used WebAuthn as their sole second factor (no TOTP enrolled) and signed in through an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider. **What broke:** WebAuthn is intended to protect accounts when another credential (such as a password or a compromised identity provider session) is known or stolen. On the affected OAuth paths, that protection was not applied. Password-based login continued to enforce the passkey challenge as expected. | Path | Scenario | Consequence | |------|----------|-------------| | Linked-identity OAuth callback | Attacker authenticates with a victim's already-linked external identity | Full session without WebAuthn challenge | | OAuth account-link sign-in | Attacker links an external identity to a victim account using the victim's password | Full session without WebAuthn challenge; external identity permanently linked to the victim account | The account-link path was the more serious case: a successful sign-in could bind the attacker's identity provider account to the victim's Gitea account. Subsequent OAuth sign-ins through that provider might no longer require the victim's password, and password rotation alone might not revoke that access. This issue is separate from [CVE-2026-20779](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-20779), which addressed TOTP replay timing. This advisory concerns which second factors the OAuth sign-in paths considered before granting a session. ## Root Cause OAuth sign-in handlers determined whether second-factor verification was required by consulting TOTP enrollment only (`GetTwoFactorByUID`). WebAuthn credentials are stored separately and were not checked on those paths before a session was issued. The password login handler already checked both TOTP and WebAuthn enrollment and redirected to the WebAuthn challenge when appropriate. A combined helper (`HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn`) existed in the codebase but was not used to gate session creation on the affected OAuth handlers. **Affected components:** - `routers/web/auth/oauth.go` — linked-identity callback (`handleOAuth2SignIn`) - `routers/web/auth/linkaccount.go` — account-link sign-in (`oauth2LinkAccount`) **Reference implementation (correct behavior):** - `routers/web/auth/auth.go` — password login path

CVE-2026-59774.title: Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read can lead to RCE
CVE-2026-59774.description: ### Summary An unauthenticated remote attacker can submit Org-mode markup containing a #+INCLUDE directive to POST /{owner}/{repo}/markup for any suitable public repository to read arbitrary server files. By extracting INTERNAL_TOKEN from app.ini, they can inject a Git hook through the internal logger and achieve command execution as the Gitea OS user during an anonymous clone. ### Details Gitea registers `POST /{username}/{reponame}/markup` with optional sign-in, repository assignment, and a repository-unit reader check. An anonymous user passes that check for a public repository with a normal readable code unit. The handler passes the supplied `Mode`, `Text`, and `FilePath` into Gitea's generic markup renderer. Selecting `Mode: file` and a `.org` filename chooses the Org-mode renderer. Gitea 1.27.0 initializes `go-org` using `org.New()` and does not replace its default `ReadFile` callback. In `go-org` 1.9.1, that callback is `ioutil.ReadFile`; `#+INCLUDE` accepts absolute paths and passes them directly to that callback. #### Preconditions - At least one repository is publicly readable and exposes a unit accepted by the repository markup route. A normal public repository with its code unit enabled satisfies this condition. - Standard Gitea storage permissions allow the service user to update Gitea's managed global Git configuration. ### Impact - Read arbitrary files accessible to the Gitea service user without an account. - Submit the file-read payload directly through a public repository's web markup route without committing a file or obtaining repository write access. - Expose Gitea configuration, internal bearer tokens, OAuth/JWT material, and deployment metadata ### Affected - The vulnerable version seem v1.22.1 ~ v1.27.0 ### Credit Found by @xbow-security. Triaged by Guido Leo <guido.leo@xbow.com>. Independently reported by https://github.com/NightRang3r

CVE-2026-60010.title: Repo-side team-link endpoint still bypasses RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess
CVE-2026-60010.description: ### Summary `PUT /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/teams/{team}` allows a non-owner repository admin to attach organization teams to a repository even when the organization has disabled that behaviour with `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess=false`. An earlier advisory fixed the corresponding team-side endpoint; the repository-side endpoint retained the weaker check. ### Details The repository-side handler's exception relies on a repository permission check (`IsOwner()`), which for an organization repository is satisfied by a user promoted to owner-level access through an attached admin team. The fixed team-side endpoint instead checks actual organization ownership when `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess` is disabled. The matching web collaboration-settings handler had the same weak check. ### Impact A user with delegated admin rights on one organization repository can grant other organization teams read or write access to that repository without approval from an actual organization owner, exposing private source and history and, for a write-capable team, granting push access. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39046, #39058). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-60018.title: Authenticated DoS in OneDev migration via unbounded version response body
CVE-2026-60018.description: ### Summary The OneDev migration downloader reads the entire `/~api/version/server` response body into memory before validating the version string, and the migration HTTP client has no timeout. A malicious OneDev-compatible server can return a very large or never-ending response. ### Details Reachable from the web, API and background-task migration paths. Reachable by any authenticated user who can start a repository migration. ### Impact Authenticated availability. An attacker who can start migrations against a server they control can force Gitea to read arbitrarily large response bodies, hold migration requests and workers open until timeout or cancellation, retain that data in memory, and exhaust the migration worker pool. On constrained deployments this creates memory pressure and a possible out-of-memory condition. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.16.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39024, #39033). ### Workarounds Restrict repository-migration permission to trusted users. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-63792.title: Fork pull requests can read reusable workflow files from another private repository (missed sibling of GHSA-fj8v-hjwv-qm88)
CVE-2026-63792.description: ### Summary `CanReadWorkflowCrossRepo` decides whether an Actions run may read a reusable workflow file referenced from another repository. Its 'collaborative owner' branch grants cross-repository read through the collaborative-owner trust relationship without checking whether the run is a fork pull request. An earlier advisory fixed the same class of flaw in a sibling function but did not touch this one. ### Details A fork pull request opened against private repository A (no write access to A required) can read reusable workflow file contents of a different private repository B, at any git ref, provided A is private, B's Actions configuration lists A's owner as a collaborative owner (a normal use of the reusable-workflow sharing feature), and the fork pull request run is approved and runs. The workflow file path is confined to the configured workflow directories, but the git ref is caller-controlled. ### Impact Read-only disclosure of private reusable workflow file contents. No write access or code execution is granted by this issue. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-66877.title: RCE on self-hosted runners | fork-PR approval gate (`NeedApproval`) bypass via job-level concurrency cancellation
CVE-2026-66877.description: ### Summary Workflow runs from first-time fork contributors are held for maintainer approval only by inserting the run's jobs in a blocked state. The component that transitions blocked jobs to waiting does not re-check whether the run still needs approval. A separate, legitimate run in the same repository that shares a job-level `concurrency` group with the pending run can cause the pending run to be re-evaluated, which unblocks and dispatches its remaining jobs to runners without approval. Any user who can open a pull request can reach this. ### Details The approval decision itself is correct, but it is enforced purely as job status. The job emitter, the concurrency-preparation path and the runner task-pickup path do not check approval; only the concurrency-wake path did. Cancelling one job of the pending run through the shared job-level concurrency group triggers a re-emit over that run's still-blocked sibling jobs, which are then moved to waiting and picked up by runners. ### Impact Arbitrary, unreviewed workflow code execution on the self-hosted runners of any repository that accepts fork pull requests, defeating the first-time-contributor approval boundary. Fork pull request secrets remain withheld and the run token remains read-only; the impact is access to the runner host (internal network reachability, runner-local caches, workspaces and credentials, and persistence into later trusted builds). ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-71184.title: Gitea Actions: fork pull request approval bypass via `pull_request_review_comment` (missing `WithPullRequest`)
CVE-2026-71184.description: ### Summary Gitea requires maintainer approval before running fork pull request workflows when the author lacks Actions write on the base repository. That gate is skipped for the `pull_request_review_comment` event (the same code path also covers review approved/rejected), because the review notifier does not attach the pull request to the notification. With no pull request attached the run is not recognized as a fork pull request and approval is not required, while the workflow definition is still loaded from the fork head and run on the base repository's runners. ### Details The sibling review-request notifier does attach the pull request; the review notifier does not. Present since the fork pull request approval gate was introduced in Gitea 1.20.0. An actor needs to be able to fork the repository, open a fork pull request, and submit a review with a line comment; they do not need Actions write on the base repository or a runner on the fork. ### Impact Unapproved execution of attacker-controlled workflow code on the base repository's runners. On a privileged or host runner this is code execution as the runner user, with possible access to secrets depending on event rules; on a sandboxed runner it is unauthorized CI/compute use. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.20.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73130.title: Unbounded gitignores repository-creation field enables linear template-read amplification
CVE-2026-73130.description: ### Summary The `gitignores` field of the repository-creation form and API option struct has no maximum-length constraint. During repository initialization the field is split on commas and each name triggers a template read whose result is buffered in memory before `.gitignore` is written. A large attacker-controlled value therefore produces a proportional number of template reads and in-memory buffering. ### Details Reachable through `POST /repo/create` and `POST /api/v1/user/repos` (and the organization equivalent) when auto-init is enabled. ### Impact Uncontrolled resource consumption during repository creation, proportional to the submitted field length. Availability only. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39027, #39040). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73273.title: Package size quota bypass and unbounded memory read in the Maven checksum upload path
CVE-2026-73273.description: ### Summary When a Maven artifact is uploaded with a checksum extension (`.md5`, `.sha1`, `.sha256`, `.sha512`), the handler reads the entire request body into memory and compares it to the stored digest, then returns — before the code path that enforces the package size quota. The checksum branch therefore has neither a size quota nor any bound on how much is read into memory, although a valid checksum value is at most 128 bytes. ### Details The body is read with `io.ReadAll` and copied again for the comparison; both allocations are sized by the client. The configured `LIMIT_SIZE_MAVEN` is not applied to this path. Reachable by any authenticated user with Maven package write access. ### Impact Package size-quota bypass and client-controlled memory allocation for a single request (uncontrolled resource consumption). A practical outage was not demonstrated; the issue should be read as an unbounded allocation and a quota bypass. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39028, #39031). ### Workarounds Limit request body size at the reverse proxy. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73278.title: WebAuthn second factor is bypassed on OAuth2/OpenID sign-in (WebAuthn-only users)
CVE-2026-73278.description: Gitea's OAuth2 and OpenID Connect sign-in flows did not enforce WebAuthn when it was a user's only configured second factor. Users who registered a passkey without TOTP were correctly challenged on password login, but could receive a full authenticated session through OAuth sign-in with no WebAuthn prompt. Two OAuth-related code paths were affected. One of them could also persist an external identity link during sign-in, extending the impact beyond a single session. ## Affected Versions All versions up to and including **1.27.0** that support WebAuthn and OAuth2/OpenID sign-in. ## Impact **Who was affected:** Users who used WebAuthn as their sole second factor (no TOTP enrolled) and signed in through an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider. **What broke:** WebAuthn is intended to protect accounts when another credential (such as a password or a compromised identity provider session) is known or stolen. On the affected OAuth paths, that protection was not applied. Password-based login continued to enforce the passkey challenge as expected. | Path | Scenario | Consequence | |------|----------|-------------| | Linked-identity OAuth callback | Attacker authenticates with a victim's already-linked external identity | Full session without WebAuthn challenge | | OAuth account-link sign-in | Attacker links an external identity to a victim account using the victim's password | Full session without WebAuthn challenge; external identity permanently linked to the victim account | The account-link path was the more serious case: a successful sign-in could bind the attacker's identity provider account to the victim's Gitea account. Subsequent OAuth sign-ins through that provider might no longer require the victim's password, and password rotation alone might not revoke that access. This issue is separate from [CVE-2026-20779](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-20779), which addressed TOTP replay timing. This advisory concerns which second factors the OAuth sign-in paths considered before granting a session. ## Root Cause OAuth sign-in handlers determined whether second-factor verification was required by consulting TOTP enrollment only (`GetTwoFactorByUID`). WebAuthn credentials are stored separately and were not checked on those paths before a session was issued. The password login handler already checked both TOTP and WebAuthn enrollment and redirected to the WebAuthn challenge when appropriate. A combined helper (`HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn`) existed in the codebase but was not used to gate session creation on the affected OAuth handlers. **Affected components:** - `routers/web/auth/oauth.go` — linked-identity callback (`handleOAuth2SignIn`) - `routers/web/auth/linkaccount.go` — account-link sign-in (`oauth2LinkAccount`) **Reference implementation (correct behavior):** - `routers/web/auth/auth.go` — password login path

CVE-2026-59774.title: Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read can lead to RCE
CVE-2026-59774.description: ### Summary An unauthenticated remote attacker can submit Org-mode markup containing a #+INCLUDE directive to POST /{owner}/{repo}/markup for any suitable public repository to read arbitrary server files. By extracting INTERNAL_TOKEN from app.ini, they can inject a Git hook through the internal logger and achieve command execution as the Gitea OS user during an anonymous clone. ### Details Gitea registers `POST /{username}/{reponame}/markup` with optional sign-in, repository assignment, and a repository-unit reader check. An anonymous user passes that check for a public repository with a normal readable code unit. The handler passes the supplied `Mode`, `Text`, and `FilePath` into Gitea's generic markup renderer. Selecting `Mode: file` and a `.org` filename chooses the Org-mode renderer. Gitea 1.27.0 initializes `go-org` using `org.New()` and does not replace its default `ReadFile` callback. In `go-org` 1.9.1, that callback is `ioutil.ReadFile`; `#+INCLUDE` accepts absolute paths and passes them directly to that callback. #### Preconditions - At least one repository is publicly readable and exposes a unit accepted by the repository markup route. A normal public repository with its code unit enabled satisfies this condition. - Standard Gitea storage permissions allow the service user to update Gitea's managed global Git configuration. ### Impact - Read arbitrary files accessible to the Gitea service user without an account. - Submit the file-read payload directly through a public repository's web markup route without committing a file or obtaining repository write access. - Expose Gitea configuration, internal bearer tokens, OAuth/JWT material, and deployment metadata ### Affected - The vulnerable version seem v1.22.1 ~ v1.27.0 ### Credit Found by @xbow-security. Triaged by Guido Leo <guido.leo@xbow.com>. Independently reported by https://github.com/NightRang3r

CVE-2026-60010.title: Repo-side team-link endpoint still bypasses RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess
CVE-2026-60010.description: ### Summary `PUT /api/v1/repos/{owner}/{repo}/teams/{team}` allows a non-owner repository admin to attach organization teams to a repository even when the organization has disabled that behaviour with `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess=false`. An earlier advisory fixed the corresponding team-side endpoint; the repository-side endpoint retained the weaker check. ### Details The repository-side handler's exception relies on a repository permission check (`IsOwner()`), which for an organization repository is satisfied by a user promoted to owner-level access through an attached admin team. The fixed team-side endpoint instead checks actual organization ownership when `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess` is disabled. The matching web collaboration-settings handler had the same weak check. ### Impact A user with delegated admin rights on one organization repository can grant other organization teams read or write access to that repository without approval from an actual organization owner, exposing private source and history and, for a write-capable team, granting push access. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39046, #39058). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-60018.title: Authenticated DoS in OneDev migration via unbounded version response body
CVE-2026-60018.description: ### Summary The OneDev migration downloader reads the entire `/~api/version/server` response body into memory before validating the version string, and the migration HTTP client has no timeout. A malicious OneDev-compatible server can return a very large or never-ending response. ### Details Reachable from the web, API and background-task migration paths. Reachable by any authenticated user who can start a repository migration. ### Impact Authenticated availability. An attacker who can start migrations against a server they control can force Gitea to read arbitrarily large response bodies, hold migration requests and workers open until timeout or cancellation, retain that data in memory, and exhaust the migration worker pool. On constrained deployments this creates memory pressure and a possible out-of-memory condition. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.16.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39024, #39033). ### Workarounds Restrict repository-migration permission to trusted users. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-63792.title: Fork pull requests can read reusable workflow files from another private repository (missed sibling of GHSA-fj8v-hjwv-qm88)
CVE-2026-63792.description: ### Summary `CanReadWorkflowCrossRepo` decides whether an Actions run may read a reusable workflow file referenced from another repository. Its 'collaborative owner' branch grants cross-repository read through the collaborative-owner trust relationship without checking whether the run is a fork pull request. An earlier advisory fixed the same class of flaw in a sibling function but did not touch this one. ### Details A fork pull request opened against private repository A (no write access to A required) can read reusable workflow file contents of a different private repository B, at any git ref, provided A is private, B's Actions configuration lists A's owner as a collaborative owner (a normal use of the reusable-workflow sharing feature), and the fork pull request run is approved and runs. The workflow file path is confined to the configured workflow directories, but the git ref is caller-controlled. ### Impact Read-only disclosure of private reusable workflow file contents. No write access or code execution is granted by this issue. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-66877.title: RCE on self-hosted runners | fork-PR approval gate (`NeedApproval`) bypass via job-level concurrency cancellation
CVE-2026-66877.description: ### Summary Workflow runs from first-time fork contributors are held for maintainer approval only by inserting the run's jobs in a blocked state. The component that transitions blocked jobs to waiting does not re-check whether the run still needs approval. A separate, legitimate run in the same repository that shares a job-level `concurrency` group with the pending run can cause the pending run to be re-evaluated, which unblocks and dispatches its remaining jobs to runners without approval. Any user who can open a pull request can reach this. ### Details The approval decision itself is correct, but it is enforced purely as job status. The job emitter, the concurrency-preparation path and the runner task-pickup path do not check approval; only the concurrency-wake path did. Cancelling one job of the pending run through the shared job-level concurrency group triggers a re-emit over that run's still-blocked sibling jobs, which are then moved to waiting and picked up by runners. ### Impact Arbitrary, unreviewed workflow code execution on the self-hosted runners of any repository that accepts fork pull requests, defeating the first-time-contributor approval boundary. Fork pull request secrets remain withheld and the run token remains read-only; the impact is access to the runner host (internal network reachability, runner-local caches, workspaces and credentials, and persistence into later trusted builds). ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-71184.title: Gitea Actions: fork pull request approval bypass via `pull_request_review_comment` (missing `WithPullRequest`)
CVE-2026-71184.description: ### Summary Gitea requires maintainer approval before running fork pull request workflows when the author lacks Actions write on the base repository. That gate is skipped for the `pull_request_review_comment` event (the same code path also covers review approved/rejected), because the review notifier does not attach the pull request to the notification. With no pull request attached the run is not recognized as a fork pull request and approval is not required, while the workflow definition is still loaded from the fork head and run on the base repository's runners. ### Details The sibling review-request notifier does attach the pull request; the review notifier does not. Present since the fork pull request approval gate was introduced in Gitea 1.20.0. An actor needs to be able to fork the repository, open a fork pull request, and submit a review with a line comment; they do not need Actions write on the base repository or a runner on the fork. ### Impact Unapproved execution of attacker-controlled workflow code on the base repository's runners. On a privileged or host runner this is code execution as the runner user, with possible access to secrets depending on event rules; on a sandboxed runner it is unauthorized CI/compute use. ### Affected versions Gitea `>= 1.20.0, <= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39005, #39018). ### Workarounds Instances that do not run fork pull request workflows on self-hosted runners are not exposed to the code-execution impact. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73130.title: Unbounded gitignores repository-creation field enables linear template-read amplification
CVE-2026-73130.description: ### Summary The `gitignores` field of the repository-creation form and API option struct has no maximum-length constraint. During repository initialization the field is split on commas and each name triggers a template read whose result is buffered in memory before `.gitignore` is written. A large attacker-controlled value therefore produces a proportional number of template reads and in-memory buffering. ### Details Reachable through `POST /repo/create` and `POST /api/v1/user/repos` (and the organization equivalent) when auto-init is enabled. ### Impact Uncontrolled resource consumption during repository creation, proportional to the submitted field length. Availability only. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39027, #39040). ### Workarounds None. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73273.title: Package size quota bypass and unbounded memory read in the Maven checksum upload path
CVE-2026-73273.description: ### Summary When a Maven artifact is uploaded with a checksum extension (`.md5`, `.sha1`, `.sha256`, `.sha512`), the handler reads the entire request body into memory and compares it to the stored digest, then returns — before the code path that enforces the package size quota. The checksum branch therefore has neither a size quota nor any bound on how much is read into memory, although a valid checksum value is at most 128 bytes. ### Details The body is read with `io.ReadAll` and copied again for the comparison; both allocations are sized by the client. The configured `LIMIT_SIZE_MAVEN` is not applied to this path. Reachable by any authenticated user with Maven package write access. ### Impact Package size-quota bypass and client-controlled memory allocation for a single request (uncontrolled resource consumption). A practical outage was not demonstrated; the issue should be read as an unbounded allocation and a quota bypass. ### Affected versions Gitea `<= 1.27.2`. ### Patches Fixed in Gitea 1.27.3 (#39028, #39031). ### Workarounds Limit request body size at the reverse proxy. Upgrade to 1.27.3.

CVE-2026-73278.title: WebAuthn second factor is bypassed on OAuth2/OpenID sign-in (WebAuthn-only users)
CVE-2026-73278.description: Gitea's OAuth2 and OpenID Connect sign-in flows did not enforce WebAuthn when it was a user's only configured second factor. Users who registered a passkey without TOTP were correctly challenged on password login, but could receive a full authenticated session through OAuth sign-in with no WebAuthn prompt. Two OAuth-related code paths were affected. One of them could also persist an external identity link during sign-in, extending the impact beyond a single session. ## Affected Versions All versions up to and including **1.27.0** that support WebAuthn and OAuth2/OpenID sign-in. ## Impact **Who was affected:** Users who used WebAuthn as their sole second factor (no TOTP enrolled) and signed in through an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider. **What broke:** WebAuthn is intended to protect accounts when another credential (such as a password or a compromised identity provider session) is known or stolen. On the affected OAuth paths, that protection was not applied. Password-based login continued to enforce the passkey challenge as expected. | Path | Scenario | Consequence | |------|----------|-------------| | Linked-identity OAuth callback | Attacker authenticates with a victim's already-linked external identity | Full session without WebAuthn challenge | | OAuth account-link sign-in | Attacker links an external identity to a victim account using the victim's password | Full session without WebAuthn challenge; external identity permanently linked to the victim account | The account-link path was the more serious case: a successful sign-in could bind the attacker's identity provider account to the victim's Gitea account. Subsequent OAuth sign-ins through that provider might no longer require the victim's password, and password rotation alone might not revoke that access. This issue is separate from [CVE-2026-20779](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-20779), which addressed TOTP replay timing. This advisory concerns which second factors the OAuth sign-in paths considered before granting a session. ## Root Cause OAuth sign-in handlers determined whether second-factor verification was required by consulting TOTP enrollment only (`GetTwoFactorByUID`). WebAuthn credentials are stored separately and were not checked on those paths before a session was issued. The password login handler already checked both TOTP and WebAuthn enrollment and redirected to the WebAuthn challenge when appropriate. A combined helper (`HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn`) existed in the codebase but was not used to gate session creation on the affected OAuth handlers. **Affected components:** - `routers/web/auth/oauth.go` — linked-identity callback (`handleOAuth2SignIn`) - `routers/web/auth/linkaccount.go` — account-link sign-in (`oauth2LinkAccount`) **Reference implementation (correct behavior):** - `routers/web/auth/auth.go` — password login path
